commits.summary: Add the private archive of original outputs: spool, journal, verified upload, list and fetch
commits.body:
llm-dlc/tools/artifacts.py is the first piece of the process-plumbing brief (llm-dlc/loops/llm-dlc-process-plumbing.md, section 2). A producer hands the bytes it made to capture before it shortens, replaces or deletes them. They are sealed once into a spool on disk outside the checkout (~/.local/share/in-the-loop/originals), with a full private inventory of every member's path, type, mode, length and SHA-256, and acknowledged only after the intake record and a SQLite journal have them durably. Small files go into bounded packs, large ones into parts, and an append-only file into segments from which any past prefix restores. A restartable uploader commits each attempt before a byte moves, creates each object only if none is there, reads it back with a credential and compares the original bytes with their name, and writes an immutable receipt last, so a fresh machine can rebuild the catalog from the store alone. Ordinary and restricted originals go to separate private R2 buckets; a restricted occurrence is listed in the ordinary one by a stub with no path. list, show and fetch read with the reader's token into a private cache and work offline on a verified hit; missing, pending, restricted or damaged evidence gives a specific unavailable answer. Nothing in the tool deletes a byte, and ITL_ORIGINALS_OFF=1 switches capture off.

Verified by 33 unit tests (llm-dlc/tools/test_artifacts.py): crashes before and after the intake record, after a put and before the receipt, a lease left by a dead worker, two workers on one object, a store that is offline, that loses its answer, that holds other bytes under the same key or a truncated object, a full disk, reused paths, gaps, unsafe manifests and links, and reads from an empty cache and offline. artifacts.py canary passed 11 of 11 checks on the real buckets on 2026-11-21: custody for both classes, a restore from an empty cache, and each token's limits (the ordinary token refused a restricted key, a PUT and a DELETE; the public Worker and the public traces' token read neither class). The contract is in llm-dlc/specification.md, Original outputs; llm-dlc/loops/llm-dlc-process-plumbing-results.md records where the run stands. Nothing calls capture yet: the runner and collector adapters come next.

commits.summary: Seal each verification run's originals before the pipeline cuts or removes them (shadow mode)
commits.body:
verification/capture.py hands what the runner and the collector produce to the private archive (llm-dlc/tools/artifacts.py) at the points where an original was lost until now: the whole step logs before they are cut to head and tail, the outputs with the declared ones that never materialized and the ones deleted, the whole changes.diff, what a failed job's work directory holds beyond its commit, the result as the runner wrote it, a collected result that a later collect replaces, a result staged by a runner that sealed nothing, and the result as collected with its conflicts. A run directory left by an attempt whose runner was killed is sealed as partial before the retry reuses its path, and each run of a job is a numbered attempt. result.json names the attempt and the occurrence ids under a new originals field (in the schema).

It is a shadow of the pipeline: verification/results holds what it held before, pipeline.py gains four calls and a loader, and a capture that fails (a full disk, say) fails no job and no collect, is said on stderr and in .state/capture.log, and makes collect set a staged result aside under .state/uncaptured instead of deleting it. The test runner and test_pipeline.py set ITL_ORIGINALS_OFF=1, so no test seals anything into this machine's archive. artifacts.capture gained sparse, for the work directory's rule.

Verified by verification/test_capture.py (7 tests, each running the pipeline in a throwaway repository with its own spool and store): the middle of a log the result cut restores byte for byte from a fresh cache; a failed job's outputs, diff and work-directory additions restore, and its never-made output is recorded; collect seals the result it replaces and the one it writes, with conflicts; a disk-full capture leaves the job passed, the collect done and the staged files set aside. The tests the change selects passed (35 files, after updating the one that pins the runner's environment). verification/README.md, Originals, describes it.

commits.summary: Inventory and protect what exists only on this VM; upload sealed originals in parallel
commits.body:
llm-dlc/tools/vm_inventory.py is the brief's first step. measure prints numbers fit to publish (heads, unpushed commits, git and jj sizes, tracked files and the widest directories, the runner's state, transcripts, run records, what a push would send, the archive's custody), to be compared before and after each change to the plumbing. pin writes a git ref under refs/itl/pins/ for every local head origin lacks, a namespace jj neither imports nor moves. protect seals into the private archive the runner's run directories and kept work directories, the loops' private run records, the project's source transcripts (Claude Code's and Codex's, as append-only streams, with their side files) and the records of examples 340 to 359, and does not seal twice what has not changed. It names only this repository's folders: no other project's sessions, credential store or dependency cache is read.

On 2026-11-21 it sealed 1,182 occurrences on this VM in two minutes: 3.21 GB of originals as 541 MB in 2,522 objects, among them 910 run directories and the 23,000 record files of runs 5 to 7, whole, before any trim (VF-053). All 8 local heads are pinned. llm-dlc/loops/llm-dlc-process-plumbing-results.md has the measurements, what was left unsealed and why, and the known historical gaps.

The uploader now works on up to 8 threads, each with its own journal connection, writes an intent for each new occurrence first, and reads back every object and every receipt; upload --drain runs passes until nothing is left to do now, as the spool's one uploader (a lock), and artifacts.kick starts one in the background when a run or a collect seals something, so the transfer off the machine starts then. Verified by three new tests in test_artifacts.py (12 occurrences on 4 threads, each object put once; the lock; the kick's switches), test_vm_inventory.py (sealed once, again only on change; a dry run seals nothing; only this repository's transcript folders are named), and the tests the change selects (5 files, test_pipeline.py among them).

commits.summary: Add sync.py checkpoint: one committed revision to origin's develop, forward only, with outgoing-object checks
commits.body:
llm-dlc/tools/checkpoint.py gives code checkpoints a job of their own, apart from promotion (the brief, section 1). sync.py checkpoint --rev REV resolves REV once to one committed revision, reads the remote's develop and main, and pushes exactly SHA:refs/heads/develop to origin when develop can move forward to it, carrying the commit develop was read at so the push cannot land on a branch that moved. It runs no test, renders no trace file, uploads no log and waits for no job or uploader, and every jj call it makes ignores the working copy, so another session's uncommitted files are neither snapshotted nor moved. --bootstrap creates develop where main is. Any other ref, remote, pattern or force is refused as an argument.

Before anything leaves the machine it reads every git object and commit message the push would expose for the first time, through every outgoing commit and merge parent, and refuses an unresolved conflict, a raw payload path, an unsafe file name, a blob over 16 MiB, a message-less or set-aside commit, a recognisable credential or one of this machine's own secrets or account identifiers anywhere, anything the redactor would still change in a trace file, and a redaction decision no person is recorded as having taken. A scan of the 18 commits then unpushed showed why the context-shaped kinds are refused in trace files only: the home path and the user name occur in 5,153 result and receipt files of the kind main already publishes, and KEY=value in 109 ordinary fixtures. A blob's verdict is kept by its git id under the policy, rules and decisions in force. A push whose answer is lost is settled by reading the remote. The receipt, outside the tree and sealed into the private archive, says which trace logs are public and which pending and what the archive holds on this machine only. After a push, develop@origin counts among jj's immutable heads.

The redactor now also treats the private archive's three R2 tokens as this machine's secrets. Verified by llm-dlc/tools/test_checkpoint.py, 12 tests on real jj repositories with a bare remote: a dirty workspace is checkpointed at its last commit with the foreign files' hashes and the working-copy commit unchanged, a fresh clone reads the code at develop, and the test gate, the session sync and the log upload are each patched to fail if called; a credential in a parent commit is refused though the tip deleted it; an unsafe message, a run record, an environment file, an oversized blob, a bad name, a conflict and a forged allow-list approval are refused with the remote unchanged; --all, --bookmark, --force, --remote, a refspec and a pattern exit 2; a develop that moved elsewhere is never forced; a lost answer is one push. The tests the change selects passed (22 files). llm-dlc/specification.md, Checkpoints, is the contract. The first push to the real develop is the watcher's, at this cycle's end (the user's decision); a rehearsal on the real history against a bare remote follows. The allow list gains one proposal (a82875ef, a made-up home directory in test_vm_inventory.py), for the user to approve.
